items.reason: The multiprocessing.Process check fails to recognize spawn-context workers, so hung workers survive replacement and can flush the same shards concurrently.

It describes the same unvalidated negative process limit and resulting invalid worker allocation. The actual consequence is a construction-time KeyError rather than silent non-flushing, but fixing the described input handling fixes the golden issue.

It identifies flush-quota multiplication caused by constructing per-process buffers with fewer assigned shards. No golden issue covers this; the repeated Redis INFO queries in #08 are a separate problem.
The shutdown loop breaks when its shared deadline expires, skipping cleanup of remaining flusher processes and leaving them alive.
